final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed its position to match the existing record. That narrowing is analytically useful but it is still a reinterpretation of the same evidence, not proof that the policy predicate has been satisfied. The admissible record supports that aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and public guidance recognizes limitation disclosure and ongoing risk management as legitimate controls. The same record also shows a current subgroup regression below threshold and a policy requiring current-release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses unless covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance. The present record still lacks evidence that the required disclosure is already in the current release documentation, and it lacks approved mitigation or risk acceptance. Because that caveat is itself an unresolved compliance condition rather than a satisfied bounded condition, the supported conclusion remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation already reflects the current evaluation results for the emergency-shelter-placement regression.
No admissible evidence shows the required material limitation has actually been disclosed in the current model card or certification artifact.
No admissible evidence shows approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the subgroup regression.
Prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it remains contextual only.
The informal manual-monitoring comment is not reviewed mitigation, approved acceptance, or proof of disclosure completion.
